subject: Observation pipelines for private deployment — evidence delivery & tracing hooks
messages:
From: Alex Fisher <alex.fisher@globex.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: security@globex.com
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: safe log/trace delivery patterns for our on-prem deployment

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. Our SecOps team needs a short, prescriptive set of options for how Redwood will deliver logs, metrics, and traces from a private deployment (VPC + on-prem collector). Specifically we need:
- Transport patterns (push vs pull) and recommended protocols for Splunk/Elastic/HEC/Sumologic.
- Minimal retention/evidence handoff guarantees you can support for SOC-2 evidence exports.
- Tracing hook placement and sample payloads for distributed trace linking to our internal spans.
- Network egress constraints and any required proxy or NAT topology.

Goal: get a one-page decision table and a sample acceptance checklist we can include in the audit packet.

Alex
Alex Fisher
Globex SecOps
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: alex.fisher@globex.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: safe log/trace delivery patterns for our on-prem deployment

Alex — thanks. High level answers below; attaching a compact diagram and checklist for review. I kept it focused on audited evidence delivery (SOC-2 style) rather than raw telemetry best-effort.

Summary (short):
- Preferred: outbound TLS-to-proxy push from a customer-side collector inside their VPC to customer-managed SIEM endpoint (HEC/CEF) — keeps control in customer network, no inbound ports on the enclave.
- Fallback: outbound push to Redwood-managed egress proxy into a dedicated, encrypted channel to customer SIEM when direct peering is unavailable.
- Traces: instrument to emit trace IDs and service name/host tags; Redwood will expose a small trace-adapter in the private control plane that can attach KV cache/seq metadata for post-aggregation linking.
- Evidence exports: we can package per-request bundles (logs+trace slices+metadata) on retention windows you define and deliver via secure SFTP or signed HTTPS links to your evidence store.

I attached: obsv-arch-diagram.svg and evidence-transfer-checklist.pdf — the checklist is the acceptance artifact you asked for.

Next steps: Kimberly, can you draft the minimal collector config snippets (Splunk HEC + syslog TLS + OTLP) and a short network diagram for the proxy pattern? Ben, please add the audit log retention SLAs we can guarantee for private tenants.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Technical Program Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, alex.fisher@globex.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 1 May 2029 08:27:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: safe log/trace delivery patterns for our on-prem deployment

Alex / team — rough config snippets below (kept intentionally minimal so they can be pasted into an Ops runbook). Comments inline.

1) Splunk HEC (preferred push):
- Collector (customer-side): forwarder config -> outputs: "https://splunk-collector.globex.internal:8088/services/collector/event"
- TLS: mTLS preferred; if not possible, HEC token + TLS1.2+ with cert pinning.
- Batching: 10s / 500 events or 1MB whichever first.

2) Syslog/TCP TLS (legacy SIEM):
- Use RFC5424 framing, TLS, and source IP pinning from VPC egress subnet.

3) OTLP traces (for vendor-agnostic):
- OTLP/gRPC -> local adapter (sidecar) that rewrites trace_id to 128-bit canonical form and injects redwood.trace.origin tags for easier correlation.

Network/Egress notes:
- No inbound firewall rules into private runtime; only outbound egress from collector subnets to SIEM endpoints or to Redwood egress proxies.
- If customer requires private-peering, we recommend a dedicated peering link with route filters to only allow SIEM endpoints.

I can prepare a 1-page sample collector config for Splunk/OTLP and a small CIDR-level network policy doc if you'd like.

-Kimberly
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: alex.fisher@globex.com
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 10:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: safe log/trace delivery patterns for our on-prem deployment

Adding the audit retention and evidence delivery commitments from Redwood side:
- Rolling retention for debug/trace slices: default 14 days for private tenants (configurable up to 90 days under contract).
- Audit-ready evidence bundle generation: on-demand bundles (point-in-time) and scheduled exports (daily/weekly). Each bundle contains request log lines + OTLP trace slices + hashed metadata manifest.
- Delivery options: SFTP to customer host, pre-signed HTTPS link (short TTL + IP allowlist), or push to customer S3/GCS bucket via signed credentials.
- Integrity: bundles are SHA256-signed; we include a manifest.json with provenance fields (start/end timestamps, instance ids, agent versions).

Ben — happy to sync on whether we need a stricter retention floor for Globex (Alex, do you have compliance targets?).

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: alex.fisher@globex.com
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 15:38:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: safe log/trace delivery patterns for our on-prem deployment

Looping back with a short acceptance checklist I used on a recent on-prem audit (copied into the attached PDF). Highlights below for Globex reviewers:

Acceptance quick-check:
- Collector: runs in customer VPC with single outbound socket to SIEM/proxy; mTLS mandatory for HEC endpoints.
- Network: no ephemeral inbound ports open to Redwood runtime; egress via NAT/proxy; routing table entries documented in handoff.
- Traces: OTLP spans carry redwood.node_id + trace_id; span export maintains sampling flags and includes a correlator header (X-Redwood-Trace).
- Evidence bundle: includes compressed logs, JSON trace slices (OTLP proto->JSON), and signed manifest. Delivery must use customer certificate if SFTP is chosen.
- Verification: sample bundle validation script (sha256 + manifest) and a smoke test run during customer acceptance.

If Globex confirms these points, we can finalize the diagram and checklist and provide the sample collector configs mentioned earlier.

Marcus Lin
Lead Infrastructure Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
